title: Ten Aussie suburbs under 'control order' from today amid biosecurity threat
text:

 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage Ten Aussie suburbs under 'control order' from today amid biosecurity threat
 A deadly pest has been detected in Sydney, triggering a major biosecurity crackdown across 10 suburbs as authorities race to contain the threat.
 Preston Potts , Carly Bass Sun 25 October 2026 at 10:41 pm UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. A control order zone is in place from today around the fire ant detection zone in Enfield, Sydney. Source: NSW Government/Apple Maps. A biosecurity control order is now in place across 10 Sydney suburbs following the detection of invasive fire ants.
 A large nest of red imported fire ants was discovered in a shipping container at the Enfield Intermodal Logistics Centre in Sydney's inner west on September 23. Since then, authorities have been scrambling to contain the threat.
 Experts told Yahoo News the pest could cost Australia more than $2 billion a year if it spreads. Last week, residents in surrounding suburbs were told to check their backyards. 
 What Sydney suburbs are in the biosecurity control zone?
 To help monitor the spread, a 2km biosecurity control order zone will be established around the detection site from today.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It will cover parts of Enfield, Greenacre, Strathfield South, Strathfield, Belfield, Chullora, Rookwood, Croydon Park, Belmore and Lakemba.
 The control order will only apply to the movement of high-risk carrier material such as turf, mulch, soil, potted plants and heavy equipment, the NSW government said on Monday.
 Businesses within the zone will need to properly treat and handle these materials before they can be transported out of or through the designated control zone.
 "For most people, daily life will continue as normal. People can go to work, visit friends and family, and move around the area as they always do," Minister for Regional NSW Tara Moriarty said on Monday.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "The restrictions only apply to the movement of specific high-risk materials that could carry fire ants."
 Do you have a story? Contact newsroomau@yahoonews.com 
 Experts will focus their search around a 2km radius of the detection site. Source: DPIRD
 Moriarty said the control order is a "practical and targeted" approach to eradicate the invasive fire ants.
 "Now that the community have that requisite understanding of what needs to be done, it is reasonable and appropriate to now introduce the control order," she said
 "This enables a longer-term approach to monitoring and managing the fire ant risk."
 "While there have been no further detections during the initial surveillance efforts, it is important we stay vigilant" she added.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement She said human movement of materials is the primary way fire ants spread.

 Residents and businesses informed about threat of fire ants
 Since the detection in September, a community education campaign has been in place designed to educate and inform local businesses and residents about the threat of fire ants.
 It includes pop-up stands at nearby Chullora Marketplace and Bunnings, as well as a permanent community information drop-in centre set up at Strathfield Park.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement NSW Biosecurity also urged residents within the area to check their yards, median strips, driveways, and roadside guttering for signs of fire ants, which typically measure between 2mm and 6mm long, and are dark red-brown in colour.
 The location of the nest was confirmed and then treated. Source: DPIRD
 Biosecurity Control Order issued after pest detection
 Yahoo News Australia confirmed that authorities were first notified on September 25 by the federal Department of Agriculture (DAFF), which is responsible for biosecurity surveillance at the site.
 Its officers discovered the ants in an ant trap during a routine inspection, and they were subsequently treated.
 The NSW government then established an incident management team, and engaged experts from the Department of Primary Industries (DPIRD) and Queensland-based officers from the National Fire Ant Program.
 Aussies are being urged to 'leave it, snap it, call it', if they detect a fire ant. Source: Supplied
 How to respond if you spot a fire ant
 Fire ants are between 2 and 6mm long and dark red-brown in colour.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But they are more likely to be identified by their distinct nests, which are small earth mounds with no visible hole.
 Anyone living or working in the vicinity is asked to be on alert. If they suspect they've found a fire ant, they're asked to follow these three instructions:
 LEAVE IT: Do not destroy or treat the nest or try to capture ants.
 SNAP IT: Safely take a clear photo or video for identification.
 CALL IT: Call the helpline on 1800 680 244 or submit an online form.
